intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (IEKD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KLK11 gene (604434) on chromosome 19q13.41.

checks.claim: Ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (IEKD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KLK11 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We provide evidence that variants at Gly50 affecting the SP cleavage of KLK11 cause a new autosomal-dominant cornification disorder with abnormal desquamation.
checks.explanation: The heterozygous KLK11 variants cause the new autosomal dominant disorder. IEKD is the name the draft uses for it.

checks.claim: The KLK11 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.41.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified two heterozygous variants affecting Gly50 in kallikrein-related peptidase (KLK)11
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature and is not stated in the abstract, but the instructions count it as supported.

paragraphs.text: Ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma is an autosomal dominant disorder of cornification. It begins early in life as ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma. The stratum corneum is thickened and dense, which reflects abnormal desquamation (Gong et al., 2023). Large hyperkeratotic pigmented plaques on the trunk have also been reported (Takeichi et al., 2023).

checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder as an autosomal dominant cornification disorder.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) described a previously undescribed autosomal dominant cornification disorder in 3 families, 1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases. The disorder was characterized by early-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma. Patients' skin showed a thickened, dense stratum corneum, which the authors interpreted as a sign of abnormal desquamation.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing in 3 families with ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases). They identified 2 heterozygous variants in the KLK11 gene, both affecting gly50 and lying around the signal peptide cleavage site. One of them was a c.149G-A transition resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution. In overexpression systems, the variants disrupted signal peptide cleavage of KLK11. The G50E variant also caused subcellular mislocalization and reduced extracellular secretion.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) found significantly lower trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like proteolytic activity in the stratum corneum of patients with KLK11 variants. Patients also showed reduced proteolysis of desmoglein-1 and delayed breakdown of corneodesmosomes, which pointed to delayed skin desquamation.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing in 3 families with ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases) and identified 2 heterozygous variants affecting gly50 of KLK11, around the signal peptide cleavage site. One of them was a heterozygous c.149G-A transition resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution. In overexpression systems, the variants disrupted signal peptide cleavage of KLK11, and G50E caused subcellular mislocalization and reduced extracellular secretion. Mice homozygous for the equivalent Klk11 G44E change (c.131G-A) had hyperkeratosis and abnormal desquamation, partly reproducing the human phenotype.
